name: Cult of the Supreme Being
summary: The Cult of the Supreme Being was the deist civic religion Robespierre had the National Convention decree in May 1794: the French people recognise a Supreme Being and the soul's immortality, and serve him by practising the duties of man, above all hatred of tyranny and care for the unfortunate. It was meant to replace both Catholicism and the atheist Cult of Reason, to ground republican morality, and to be carried by national festivals; it kept freedom of worship while punishing disorder done in any cult's name. It ended with Robespierre's fall in July 1794.
scope: The 1794 state cult as set out in Robespierre's report of 18 Floréal Year II (7 May 1794), the decree it proposed and the Convention adopted, and the Festival of the Supreme Being of 8 June 1794, read with Cratty's scholarship on it as a form of practical deist civil religion. It excludes Rousseau's civil religion in the Social Contract, Theophilanthropy and other deist cults, and Robespierre's wider politics (the Terror, economic policy) except where the decree or the report itself makes them part of the cult.

keyFigures.role: Devised the cult and presented the report and decree to the Convention; led the festival
keyFigures.quote: Robespierre fused radical republicanism and practical civil religion to create the cult

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Article XI of the decree maintains freedom of worship, and only disorder or counter-revolutionary preaching under any cult was to be punished.

clerical-rule.rationale: Robespierre rejects priestly authority outright: priests are to morality what charlatans are to medicine, he will not restore their empire, and the true priest of the Supreme Being is Nature.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The decree sets a festival 'to the Martyrs of liberty' and to those who served the nation, and the report praises Bara and Viala as models.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The decree orders an annual state festival of 21 January 1793 (the king's execution) and of 10 August 1792, and a festival of 'hatred of tyrants and traitors'.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Convention's decree made recognition of the Supreme Being and the soul's immortality a state act, instituted national festivals under his auspices, and the state held the Festival of the Supreme Being on 8 June 1794.

patriotic-education.rationale: He wants public education common and equal, aimed at forming citizens, with the fatherland alone entitled to raise its children, and national festivals to awaken love of country.

sacred-ruler.rationale: He denounces priests who told kings they were God's images on earth, saying sceptre and censer conspired to usurp the earth, and in the festival speech that God did not create kings.

self-interest-moral.rationale: He blames materialist philosophy for 'reducing egoism to a system' and presents devotion to country and duty, not self-interest, as the republic's morality.

separate-church-state.rationale: The state itself established a civic worship (decree articles I, II, IV, XV) and the Convention presided over the festival to the Supreme Being, the opposite of strict separation.

spiritual-nature.rationale: He tells the Convention that every institution and doctrine that consoles and elevates souls should be welcomed, and the cult was designed to serve that end.

state-harmful.rationale: The cult was an institution of the republican state, created by decree of the Convention, with state committees charged to organise its festivals.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The state ceremony burned a monument to 'Atheism' to reveal Wisdom, and the decree recognised the Supreme Being as official doctrine; atheism was treated as a conspiracy to be countered, not promoted.

universal-morality.rationale: He holds that morality rests on 'eternal and sacred bases', with a moral sense planted in man by Nature and a sanction from a power above man.

missingStatements.text: A society's morality depends on belief in a supreme being.
missingStatements.rationale: Robespierre's report treats belief in a Supreme Being and the soul's immortality as the social basis of justice and warns that destroying it demoralises the people.

quotes.text: L'idée de l'Etre suprême et de l'immortalité de l'âme est un rappel continuel à la justice; elle est donc sociale et républicaine.
Il suffit même que cette opinion ait régné chez un peuple, pour qu'il soit dangereux de la détruire.

missingStatements.text: The state should hold national festivals to strengthen citizens' civic virtue.
missingStatements.rationale: The decree institutes annual national festivals and the report calls a system of them the surest means of regeneration.

quotes.text: Il sera institué des fêtes pour rappeler l'homme à la pensée de la Divinité et à la dignité de son être.

notes: Themes searched: religion and church-state, morality and education, the regime's institutions and festivals, kingship and revolution, war and foreign affairs, economy, rights and liberties, welfare. The decree and report speak mainly to religion, civic morality, education and festivals; they are silent on economics, criminal justice, gender, technology, ecology and international institutions, so those are null. Robespierre's wider politics and the Terror belong to other subjects and were not used. The Wikipedia article was used only to find the decree and its adoption date.
